slug: 2026-03-31 Africa we have a data problem

facts.fact: The author's AI-assisted country review says recording in Lesotho's rural primary schools is entirely on paper, with enrolment and attendance going on to paper Annual Statistical Census forms that principals fill and send through district officers, and digitised only centrally; no date is given, so the document's publication date is used.

The author's AI-assisted country review says it found no evidence of a school-level digital rollout in Lesotho by 2023-2026, and scores rural schools 1; no single date is given, so the document's publication date is used.

The author's AI-assisted country review says a 2017-2018 OpenEMIS pilot aimed at learner unit records was scaled back for want of district statisticians, equipment and internet; it gives no count of pilot schools.

systems.tiers: Pilot in 2017-2018, scaled back; pilot sites not stated

systems.system: OpenEMIS (central capture of the annual census)
systems.tiers: Central only: data from the paper forms is captured centrally for aggregated annual reporting, not individual tracking
Filled by school principals, submitted through district officers to the centre
Planned; the plans emphasise district-level roles

note: Passages file; the source's own header marks its country figures as an AI-aided compilation and the author's analysis, not sourced fact. It also gives about 10 of 1,477 primary schools with rudimentary ICT access, undated.
